reason: The cited evidence shows that FSP refines grains in HEAs (E3) and that CoCrFeMnNi is susceptible to hot cracking due to thermal expansion mismatch and liquid films (E1, E2). However, no evidence is provided for in situ filler injection, homogeneous dispersion, or creation of a compositional gradient that reduces thermal stresses, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Friction stir processing (FSP) can refine grains and eliminate pre-existing cracks in high-entropy alloys via dynamic recrystallization
Injected CoCrFeMnNi filler can be homogeneously dispersed to create a seamless compositional gradient
A compositional gradient minimizes thermal expansion mismatch and associated tensile stresses that cause hot cracking
CoCrFeMnNi has a high thermal expansion coefficient (~23–25 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹) that contributes to hot cracking susceptibility in fusion welding
FSP can be performed below 0.5Tm (solid-state) to avoid hot cracking
